_comment: meeting-to-crm settings. Copy to ~/.leanscale-gtm/meeting-to-crm.json — /meeting-to-crm:setup writes it for you from your real CRM schema. Every key below is followed by a _<key>_help line. Edit by hand any time; the plugin re-reads this file on every run. IMPORTANT: nothing in this file can make the plugin write. Applying always requires the --apply flag plus a named human approval, on a later turn than the proposal.
_org_name_help: Shown on the report. Falls back to profile.json org_name.
_crm_help: salesforce | hubspot. Decides the API-name conventions, the restricted-field list, and the write payload shape.
_internal_email_domains_help: Your own domains. Everyone else on the invite is treated as a customer/prospect attendee, which is how meeting-to-account matching starts.
_transcript_source_help: kind: gong | fireflies | chorus | grain | otter | zoom | google_drive | local_dir | manual. 'tool' is the MCP tool the probe resolved. 'folder_id' for google_drive, 'local_dir' for a plain directory of transcript files. See the adapter section in skills/run/SKILL.md.
_meeting_types_help: Which meetings get processed. A meeting whose type is not in 'include' is skipped entirely — no proposals, no writes. require_external_attendee drops internal-only calls even when the type looks right.
_matching_help: How a meeting is tied to a record. THIS IS THE HIGHEST-RISK STEP — a wrong match writes one customer's notes onto another customer's deal. 'min_score' is the floor for the best candidate; 'margin' is how far ahead of the runner-up it must be. Anything short of that is reported as ambiguous and produces ZERO proposals until a human resolves it. 'overrides' is the manual escape hatch: {"<meeting_id>": {"object": "Opportunity", "id": "006..."}}.
_field_allowlist_help: The ONLY fields this plugin may ever propose. A field that is not a key here is dropped before it reaches the diff, no matter how confident the model is. overwrite: 'if_blank' (default — never touch a field that already has a value), 'always' (may replace an existing value; opt in per field), 'append' (adds a dated block underneath what is already there and never deletes anything).
_restricted_fields_opt_in_help: Amount, CloseDate, StageName, Probability and ForecastCategoryName are forecast-bearing and are OFF by default even if you add them to field_allowlist. To let the agent propose one, put its fully-qualified name here — e.g. ["Opportunity.CloseDate"] — AND add it to field_allowlist. Two locks, deliberately. Most teams should leave this empty: those are the rep's call.
_read_only_fields_help: Extra fields to treat as un-writable on top of the built-in list (formula fields, roll-up summaries, HubSpot calculated properties). Setup fills this from your CRM describe.
_framework_help: Your qualification framework mapped to real field API names. name: MEDDPICC | MEDDIC | BANT | SPICED | custom. Dimensions the call never covered are reported as blanks — a blank is a correct answer and is never invented.
_child_records_help: New stakeholders heard on a call are the highest-value, lowest-risk write — they add a record instead of changing one. A proposed contact role is dropped if that person is already on the deal.
_min_confidence_help: Proposals below this confidence are dropped and listed as low-confidence rather than shown as ready to apply.
_allow_past_dates_help: false drops a proposed next-step date that lands before the meeting itself — that is always a misread, not a plan.
_max_value_length_help: Hard ceiling on any proposed value. Per-field limits from your CRM describe win when they are tighter.
_approval_help: Who may approve a batch. 'approvers' must list the humans permitted to approve writes — while require_named_approver is true an empty list refuses every write, because an approval that cannot be checked against anything is not an approval and an agent could otherwise approve its own proposals under any name. Set require_named_approver to false only in a sandbox. min_review_seconds is the floor between rendering the diff and accepting it — it exists so a batch cannot be proposed and applied in one breath.
_audit_help: Every applied write appends one JSON line per field to ~/.leanscale-gtm/audit/meeting-to-crm.log: timestamp, record, field, old value, new value, source meeting, approver. Turning this off also turns off applying — the audit log is the price of writing.
_dry_run_help: There is deliberately NO key here that turns on apply mode. Dry-run is the default and the only way to change it is the explicit --apply flag on the approve step, with a named approver and the token printed on the rendered diff.

_hubspot_example._note: Inert reference block — keys starting with _ are stripped by the loader. If crm is 'hubspot', your file should look like this instead.
